--- title: "Final phoneme deletion" subtitle: "Automatically generated task sheet · CF_SUPRESION_FONEMA_FINAL" --- ::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"} **Automatically generated task sheet** (A · Accuracy; quality class A). Generated on November 27, 2026 with `scripts/R/ficha_generica_v3.R --tarea CF_SUPRESION_FONEMA_FINAL`. Figures come from the data; the theoretical framework is shared by the tasks of the same construct. **Interpretation and team review are missing.** Spanish name: *Supresión del fonema final*. [Spanish version](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/fichas/auto/CF_SUPRESION_FONEMA_FINAL.html). ::: **In one sentence.** Final phoneme deletion, at age 5 (3,129 administrations in 5 cohorts). AUC .71–.76 against persistent reading difficulty. ## Description | | | |---|---| | Codes | 1839 | | Battery | LEEDUCA | | Format | pictures on screen | | Items | 10 (1839) according to the platform | | Task family | A · Accuracy | | Score | Correct responses | | Instructions (platform) | The experimenter names an object presented on the screen, then the child repeats the name dropping the final phoneme. The result was a word. | ## How it is programmed on the platform The platform is the reference: what the activity actually presents is what is measured. Configuration read from the activity itself on 23/10/2026 (without modifying it). Cell contents are in Spanish. | Code|Name on the platform |Presentation | Test items| Practice items|Example items |Time limit |Order |Scoring | Age.term (label 3)| |----:|:--------------------|:----------------------|----------:|--------------:|:-------------|:----------|:-----|:--------|------------------:| | 1839|Omitir fonemas |Un dibujo por pantalla | 10| 0|— |— |fijo |Aciertos | 5, 5.2, 5.3| **Differences from the dictionary or the instructions (in Spanish):** - **1839.** 10 dibujos. *Age.term: provisional reading of the activity's label 3 (3rd digit = age, 4th = term; 0 = annual), to be confirmed with the engineer.* **How it looks on the platform** (first item or example; 2026 screenshot; the interface is in Spanish). ::: {layout-ncol=1} ![1839 · Omitir fonemas](../../figuras/plataforma/1839.jpg){.lightbox width="40%" fig-alt="Screenshot of activity 1839"} ::: ## Theoretical framework Phonological awareness is the ability to reflect on and manipulate the sounds of speech. The platform's tasks cover a continuum of difficulty: - by **unit**: syllable or phoneme; - by **operation**: counting, identifying, segmenting or deleting; - by **position**: initial, final or any. The "all positions" version mixes items and is the most demanding. **What the evidence says:** - **Phonemes and manipulation are what most distinguish dyslexia.** In 2,252 children from six European languages, phoneme deletion and RAN were the strongest concurrent predictors of dyslexia [@landerl2013predictors]. In consistent orthographies, children with dyslexia perform below even younger readers of the same reading level on phoneme manipulation tasks, but not on syllable tasks [@parrila2020rlmatch]. - **In Spanish, phonological awareness develops in stages**, from the syllable to the phoneme. Phonemic awareness builds on learning to read and at the same time drives it: the relation is reciprocal [@denton2000pa]. Phonological awareness predicts above all the reading of complex syllables [@martinez2020silabica]. - **Its predictive value is universal, but changes with age.** Phonemic awareness, letters and RAN predict reading growth equally in Spanish, Czech and English [@caravolas2013growth]. Its relation with fluency, however, is more complex and depends on task and age, whereas RAN predicts fluency in all languages [@landerl2019pa]. This is what @catts2026definicion lead us to expect: precursors are useful for early prognosis and lose weight once there is reading to measure. The pilot task sheets develop this framework in more detail: [syllable counting](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/fichas/CF523.html) and [rapid naming](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/fichas/RAN.html) (*in Spanish*). **What our data show.** The pattern matches the literature: - **What predicts best.** Deletion tasks in all positions are those that best predict low Woodcock-Muñoz fluency (median AUC .72–.73, up to .81). - **In between.** The other deletion and identification tasks (.63–.68). - **What predicts least.** Phoneme segmentation and syllable counting (.60–.62). - **Consistency and stability.** Internal consistency is good (α = .82–.94), but stability between terms is low (ρ = .27–.41). Many tasks were given in only one or two sessions, and children change quickly at these ages. For an individual decision, the result should be confirmed at two time points. ## Sample and descriptive statistics | Time point| Cohort| Session|School year | N| Non-Preleo| Preleo| Schools| |----------:|------:|-------:|:-----------|---:|----------:|------:|-------:| | 5.2| 2011| 156|2016/17 | 894| 0| 894| 35| | 5.2| 2012| 187|2017/18 | 326| 323| 0| 16| | 5.2| 2013| 629|2018/19 | 667| 435| 232| 33| | 5.2| 2014| 907|2019/20 | 379| 13| 366| 20| | 5.3| 2010| 140|2015/16 | 863| 256| 605| 36| | Time point| N| Cohorts| Mean| SD| Median| Skewness| % floor| % ceiling| |----------:|---:|----------------:|----:|----:|------:|--------:|-------:|---------:| | 5.2| 771| 2012, 2013, 2014| 5.54| 3.28| 6| -0.12| 6.36| 16.60| | 5.3| 256| 2010| 5.48| 3.17| 6| -0.41| 7.03| 0.00| **Score range** (non-Preleo group, in correct responses). The usual range goes from P1 to P99 (98% of the children). The minimum–maximum is the one observed after cleaning; the possible range is 0–10 correct responses. | Time point| N|Usual range (P1–P99) |Min.–max. |Possible range | Warning| |----------:|---:|:--------------------|:---------|:--------------|-------:| | 5.2| 771|0–10 |0–10 |0–10 | | | 5.3| 256|0–9 |0–9 |0–10 | | ## Reliability There are no two time points with the same children (at least 80). α (2021) = .87. ## Validity **Concurrent.** With other tasks in its own domain (Phonological awareness), r = .54. Outside its domain, the highest relation is with: Word and text reading (5.2, r = .43); Letter knowledge (5.3, r = .46). **Against reading difficulty and comprehension.** Against persistent difficulty, AUC .71–.76. Against poor comprehension one or two school years later (non-circular criterion), AUC .59–.62. ![Validity: AUC with 95% confidence interval (labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_CF_SUPRESION_FONEMA_FINAL_F2_validez.png){width=85%} **Against an external criterion, years later.** Against low Woodcock-Muñoz reading fluency in 2021/22 ([chapter](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/criterio-woodcock.html), *in Spanish*), AUC .67–.69 (2 time points; 220–521 children). ## Provisional norms | Time point| N| Cohorts| P5| P10| P16| P25| P50| P75| P90| |----------:|---:|----------------:|--:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 5.2| 771| 2012, 2013, 2014| 0| 1| 2| 3| 6| 9| 10| | 5.3| 256| 2010| 0| 1| 1| 2| 6| 9| 9| These are norms by time point (school year × term). For dates between assessments and time points without a normative sample, study M3 proposes continuous norms on **months of instruction**, not on age, with relative age within the school year as an adjustment. ![Provisional norms (non-Preleo schools; labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_CF_SUPRESION_FONEMA_FINAL_F1_baremo.png){width=85%} ## Variables that affect it |Variable | Time point| n| Effect| p| |:---------------------------------------|----------:|-----:|------:|-----:| |School SES (ρ) | 5.2| 2,194| 0.137| 0.000| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 5.2| 2,206| -0.010| 0.819| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 5.2| 2,225| 0.134| 0.000| |School (ICC) | 5.2| 2,266| 0.155| | |School SES (ρ) | 5.3| 863| 0.159| 0.000| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 5.3| 823| 0.039| 0.576| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 5.3| 822| 0.115| 0.001| |School (ICC) | 5.3| 863| 0.180| | ## For publications The LEEDUCA platform task “Final phoneme deletion” (code 1839; LEEDUCA battery) assesses phonemic awareness (final phoneme deletion). Each item is presented with a picture on the screen; the examiner gives the instruction orally and records the child's response. It comprises 10 items. The time limit is 120 seconds. It is administered individually on a computer at school. In the 2010, 2011, 2012, 2013 and 2014 cohorts it was administered in 5 sessions, from 5 years of age. The main outcome is the number of correct responses. In our data (2021 analyses), internal consistency was α = .87 (N = 2,301, 10 items). Against later poor reading comprehension, AUC = .59–.62. ## Pending issues - Ceiling effect at 5.2 (more than 15% of children with the maximum score). - Write the interpretation; review with the team.
